title: Freya and the Ghost
premise: Paloma Okafor, a hostage negotiator whose one public failure still haunts her, is quietly loaned out to cases the government wants deniable. When a safe house she once used is listed for sale online — complete with interior photos showing her old case files — she realizes someone is selling secrets, and the trail leads to a plot disguised as an industrial accident timed for the Frankfurt market open. Working off the books with a ghost of an informant known only as 'Freya,' Paloma must decide whether loyalty to her agency or to the truth matters more. In the end she exposes the attack and burns her own career to do it, walking away from the institution that made her.
about_author: R. M. Joubert is a former crisis-line counselor who spent a decade listening to people at their worst before turning to fiction. They write from a farmhouse in the Ardennes, where the phone never rings after midnight — by rule, not luck.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Scrolling property sites at 2 a.m., she finds the safe house listed with photos of rooms only insiders ever saw — including her old evidence board. The emotional beat: cold recognition that her deniable world has become inventory.

chapters.title: Unattributed
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Her handler, Voss, denies everything but assigns her to investigate 'quietly.' She learns three other safe houses were listed in six months. Beat: professional dread masked as routine.

chapters.title: Freya
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A burner message arrives signed 'Freya' — the codename of an informant officially dead since the failure that haunts Paloma's record. Freya claims to know who's selling the houses. Beat: hope tangled with suspicion.

chapters.title: The One That Broke
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Paloma's POV. The botched negotiation two years ago: the hostage died because orders came down to stall, not save. Beat: guilt reframed as manipulation she didn't see then.

chapters.title: Open House
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, with a tense scene through the estate agent's eyes. She tours the safe house posing as a buyer and finds a hidden camera still live. Someone watches her find it. Beat: hunter realizing she's prey.

chapters.title: Dead Frequency
chapters.summary: Freya's POV (first time). The informant explains how they faked their death and has been tracing the leaks from inside a private security firm. Beat: wary alliance forming across a wire.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Opens at Nine
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Freya reveals chatter about an 'accident' scheduled for market open — a chemical release blamed on aging infrastructure, timed to crater a rival firm's stock. Beat: stakes snap into focus.

chapters.title: Chain of Custody
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. He reports Paloma's unauthorized contact upward, torn between protecting her and protecting himself. Beat: institutional rot shown from inside.

chapters.title: The Buyer
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Following the listing agent leads to a shell company tied to Meridian Capital, whose short positions against Frankfurt industrials are enormous. Beat: money as motive made visible.

chapters.title: Two Phones
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She must brief her team without revealing Freya, lying to colleagues she respects. A junior analyst, Idris, notices the gaps. Beat: isolation deepening; love-against-duty theme seeded between Paloma and Freya's trust.

chapters.title: What Freya Wants
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya admits the real goal isn't money alone — it's exposing the firm that ordered their 'death.' They ask Paloma to go fully off-book. Beat: intimacy and risk entwined.

chapters.title: Surveillance State of Mind
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. He tails Paloma on his own, half loyal, half ambitious, and photographs her meeting Freya. Beat: the net tightening from an unexpected quarter.

chapters.title: The Accident Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Recon of the target facility reveals valve tampering already underway — the 'accident' is days from ready. Beat: ticking clock engaged.

chapters.title: Orders
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. His superiors order him to shut the investigation down; the firm has friends at the top. He must choose whether to burn Paloma or join her. Beat: corruption of power personified.

chapters.title: Compromised
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Idris's photos reach Meridian; Freya's location is raided. Paloma arrives minutes late to an empty flat and a smashed burner. Beat: despair, and the first real fear for Freya's life.

chapters.title: Negotiating With Ghosts
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Using every skill she has, she talks her way into Meridian's security chief under a false pretext and learns Freya is alive, held for leverage. Beat: her failure-haunted craft finally aimed at the right target.

chapters.title: The Trade
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She offers herself and the evidence chain in exchange for Freya — a negotiation where she is the hostage. Beat: love against duty crystallized.

chapters.title: Market Open
chapters.summary: Alternating Paloma/Freya POV. The attack triggers early; Paloma, freed mid-exchange, races to trigger the failsafe while Freya broadcasts proof to regulators and press. Beat: climax — chaos, sacrifice, near-loss.

chapters.title: Aftermath Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. He chooses to publish what he photographed, ending his career prospects and saving Paloma's credibility. Beat: redemption of the watcher.

chapters.title: Hearings
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Official inquiry: she is praised in private, erased in public, and quietly dismissed. Voss resigns rather than sign the finding. Beat: bitter vindication.

chapters.title: The House Sold
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The safe house finally sells to an ordinary family; Freya watches from across the street, alive and unlisted. Beat: quiet grief and freedom.

chapters.title: New Number
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Months later, a burner buzzes with a message from Freya — not work, just a question about coffee. Paloma smiles and answers. Beat: resolution; identity rebuilt outside the institution, love chosen over duty.
